problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=-6{e}^{-2t}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=2\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}$, find the velocity (in $\text{m/s}$)  of the particle at time $t.$

feedback.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=2t-9{t}^{2}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=-2\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=1\,\text{s}$, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment $t=2\,\text{s}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (2t-9{t}^{2})\text{d}t \\  & ={t}^{2}-3{t}^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(1)=-2.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-2 & =(1)^{2}-3(1)^{3}+C \\ -2 & =1-3+C \\ C & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)={t}^{2}-3{t}^{3}.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=2\,\text{s}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(2) & =(2)^{2}-3(2)^{3} \\  & =4-24 \\  & =-20\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $20\,\text{m/s}.$
